findings.title: Making .small-action a flex container silently disables the button's float: right
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (@include flexbox()), but the still-unmodified rule at line 306-310 right-aligns the action button with `float: right;`. Per the flexbox spec, `float` is ignored on flex items, so the button is no longer pushed to the right edge of the row. Because `.small-action-desc` (line 279) has no `flex: 1` / `margin-left: auto`, it will only be as wide as its content, leaving the button sitting immediately after the description text (and at the far left when the description is empty). This changes the visual layout of every small-action row (deleted posts, etc.). Either give `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1`, add `margin-left: auto` to the button, or drop the flex change.

findings.title: `order` mixin maps order values to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group without the required +1 offset
findings.body: The 2009 box model properties `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based and must be positive integers, while the modern `order` property is 0-based and also accepts negatives. Passing `$val` straight through means `@include order(1)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 1`, which is the default and therefore a no-op, and `@include order(0)` emits an invalid value that old WebKit/Gecko discard. The current call sites (`order(2)`, `order(3)`) happen to keep the correct relative order only because the unordered `.title` implicitly stays at group 1, but the mixin is unsafe for any future use. Emit `$val + 1` for the `*-box-ordinal-group` properties.

findings.title: Removing float: right from .panel loses right alignment in non-flex / legacy-box renderers
findings.body: `.panel` previously used `float: right;` to sit at the right edge of the header. That rule was removed and replaced by `margin-left: auto;` inside the new flex `.contents` container. Auto margins on flex items are not supported by the 2009 `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` implementations (the reason those prefixed `display` values are emitted by the `flexbox` mixin), and are ignored entirely by browsers with no flex support (e.g. IE9), which is why the prefixed `display` values exist. In those renderers the panel loses its float and now flows immediately after `.title`/`.extra-info-wrapper` instead of being right-aligned, so the header layout degrades exactly in the browsers the mixin is meant to cover. Keep the float as a fallback (floats are inert inside a real flex container) or otherwise provide a fallback.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items declaration and invalid -webkit-box-align values
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property — IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted — so that line is dead code. More importantly, `-webkit-box-align` (line 118) does not accept the `baseline` value, which is exactly what the new call site in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:57` passes (`@include align-items(baseline)`). In old WebKit, where this mixin switches the element to `display: -webkit-inline-box`, the declaration is discarded and `-webkit-box-align` falls back to `stretch`, so the bullet badge children can be stretched to the line box instead of baseline-aligned; previously those browsers got the `inline-block` fallback and normal inline alignment. Consider dropping the bogus `-ms-align-items`, and either omitting `baseline` for the prefixed property or documenting that it only applies to the standard declaration.
